exposure: pulsatility index of the uterine arteries
cohort: Pregnant women (1417 initially, 1306 followed up) evaluated between 20 and 25 weeks of gestation.
finding: The study found that a higher pulsatility index of the uterine arteries, maternal age above 35, parity ≥3, chronic hypertension, and obesity (with increasing risk by grade) were all significantly associated with an increased relative risk of developing hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.
